paper: Markowska, Ahl & Naldi (2023) Timeout: the role of family-friendly policies in business start-up, Entrepreneurship Theory and Practice
why: Qualitative study of mother founders; Theunissen et al. (2026) quote it calling leave time to identify new business opportunities and a trigger. Would give both themes at founder level.

paper: Mantere, Aula, Schildt & Vaara (2013) Narrative attributions of entrepreneurial failure, Journal of Business Venturing
why: Founder-level source of Jabbouri et al.'s narrative types (Jabbouri states the routine theme but in corporate R&D). May also name failures blamed on other parties.

paper: Castello, Barbera-Tomas & Vaara (2023) Moving on: narrative identity reconstruction after entrepreneurial failure, Journal of Business Venturing
why: Founders' own retellings after failure; a founder-level source for account-19 (Jabbouri and Haynie & Shepherd state it outside founders or after trauma).

paper: Zheng & Mai (2013) A contextualized transactive memory system view on how founding teams respond to surprises, Strategic Entrepreneurship Journal
why: Defines surprises as unexpected events significant for the startup and separates threats from opportunities; the 6-anomaly theme has no stating paper yet.

paper: Johnson, Short, Chandler & Jordan (2022) Introducing the contentpreneur, Journal of Business Venturing Insights
why: Creators build an audience through content, then monetise it; most direct statement of launching to an existing following.

paper: Murray, Kotha & Fisher (2020) Community-based resource mobilization, Organization Science
why: Founders draw resources from a community built before a campaign; cited by Murray et al. (2026).

paper: Aggarwal, Gopal, Gupta & Singh (2012) Putting money where the mouths are, Information Systems Research
why: Third-party blog coverage of specific ventures, which the firm does not control, linked to funding; Greenwood & Gopal (2015) only lean on this theme.

paper: Demetry (2017) Pop-up to professional, Academy of Management Discoveries
why: Hobby chefs' local following validates them into a business; also about accounts.

paper: Wang, Song & Zhao (2014) Legitimacy and the value of early customers, Journal of Product Innovation Management
why: Early customers' endorsement as a result apart from sales; for the goodwill part of the 9-anomaly theme.

paper: Agrawal, Catalini, Goldfarb & Luo (2018) Slack time and innovation, Organization Science
why: Core slack-time evidence cited by all three time papers; the readers found those papers only lean on the theme.

paper: Carare (2012) The impact of bestseller rank on demand: evidence from the app market, International Economic Review
why: App Store rank as a visibility shock outside the developer's control (DOI not in our catalogs; check).

paper: Gartner (2007) Entrepreneurial narrative and a science of the imagination, Journal of Business Venturing
why: A founder's narrative as retrospective sensemaking; a second source beside Dimov (2011).
